examples.en: An unexpected situation came up, so the meeting was canceled.

examples.ko: 그 아이의 돌발적인 행동에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised by that child's sudden behavior.

examples.ko: 오후에 돌발적으로 비가 쏟아져서 우산이 없었어요.
examples.en: It suddenly poured in the afternoon and I had no umbrella.
She answered calmly even to the unexpected question.

examples.ko: 이번 사고는 돌발적이라서 미리 막기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: This accident was sudden, so it was hard to prevent in advance.

examples.ko: 여행 중에는 돌발적인 일이 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: Unexpected things often happen while traveling.

explain: '돌발적인 행동/상황/질문'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙이거나 '돌발적으로'로 많이 써요. '갑작스럽다'보다 예상하지 못하게 튀어나온 일이라는 느낌이 강하고, 뉴스에서는 '돌발 상황'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used before a noun, as in '돌발적인 행동/상황/질문', or as '돌발적으로'. Compared with '갑작스럽다', it feels more like something that popped up unexpectedly. In the news you also hear '돌발 상황'.

examples.ko: 저 산은 흙이 거의 없는 돌산이에요.
examples.en: That mountain is a rocky mountain with almost no soil.
Because it is a rocky mountain, trees don't grow well.
We climbed the slippery rocky mountain very carefully.

examples.ko: 멀리서 보면 이 산은 돌산처럼 보여요.
examples.en: From far away, this mountain looks like a rocky mountain.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 뒤에는 큰 돌산이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big rocky mountain behind our neighborhood.
They say the house was built with stones dug from the rocky mountain.

explain: 돌과 바위가 많고 흙이 적은 산이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '바위산'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a mountain with many stones and rocks and little soil. In everyday talk people also say '바위산'.

examples.ko: 아기 돌상에 실과 쌀과 연필을 올렸어요.
examples.en: We put thread, rice and a pencil on the baby's first-birthday table.
Setting up a first-birthday table is harder than you think.

examples.ko: 모두 돌상 앞에서 아기가 무엇을 잡을지 기다렸어요.
examples.en: Everyone waited in front of the table to see what the baby would pick.
There are also shops that rent out first-birthday tables.

examples.ko: 할머니가 돌상에 올릴 떡을 직접 만드셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother made the rice cakes for the table herself.

examples.ko: 아기가 돌상 위에 있던 돈을 집었어요.
examples.en: The baby picked up the money on the table.

explain: 아기의 첫 생일인 '돌'에 차려 주는 상이에요. 돌상 위에서 아기가 물건을 고르는 것은 '돌잡이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the table set up for a baby's first birthday, called '돌'. Picking an item from the table is called '돌잡이'.

examples.en: I had stone pot bibimbap for lunch.
If you cook rice in a stone pot, scorched rice forms at the bottom.
The stone pot is very hot, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 돌솥으로 밥을 지어 줘요.
examples.en: This restaurant cooks the rice in a stone pot.

examples.ko: 돌솥이 나올 때 지글지글 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: A sizzling sound came from the stone pot when it was brought out.

examples.ko: 돌솥에서 막 나온 밥이 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice fresh out of the stone pot is really delicious.

explain: 음식 이름 앞에 붙어 '돌솥비빔밥', '돌솥밥'처럼 많이 나와요. 열을 오래 간직해서 음식이 끝까지 따뜻하고, 밥이 눌어 누룽지가 생겨요. 흙으로 만든 '뚝배기'와 비슷하게 뜨거운 채로 나오니 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: It often appears in food names such as '돌솥비빔밥' and '돌솥밥'. It holds heat for a long time, so the food stays hot and the rice gets scorched at the bottom. Like an earthenware '뚝배기', it comes out very hot, so be careful.

examples.ko: 동생은 화가 나서 벽 쪽으로 돌아누웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was angry and turned over to face the wall.

examples.ko: 잠이 안 와서 밤새 이쪽저쪽으로 돌아누워요.
examples.en: I can't sleep, so I turn over this way and that all night.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰 수 있으니까 천천히 돌아누우세요.
examples.en: The baby might wake up, so please turn over slowly.

examples.ko: 옆으로 돌아누워서 자면 허리가 덜 아파요.
examples.en: If I sleep turned on my side, my back hurts less.

examples.ko: 그는 말없이 돌아눕더니 곧 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: He turned over without a word and soon fell asleep.

examples.ko: 옆 사람이 돌아누울 때마다 침대가 흔들려요.
examples.en: Every time the person next to me turns over, the bed shakes.

explain: 누운 채로 몸의 방향을 바꾸는 거예요. 화가 나거나 말하기 싫을 때 상대에게 등을 보이고 돌아눕는 장면으로도 자주 나와요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '돌아누워요', '돌아누웠어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It means changing the direction of your body while lying down. It often shows up in scenes where someone turns their back to another person out of anger or reluctance to talk. It is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so you get '돌아누워요' and '돌아누웠어요'.

examples.ko: 그는 의자를 돌려 창문 쪽으로 돌아앉았어요.
examples.en: He turned his chair and sat facing the window.

examples.ko: 친구가 화가 나서 저를 등지고 돌아앉아요.
examples.en: My friend is angry and sits with their back to me.
It is more comfortable to talk when we turn around and sit facing each other.
The child is sulking and sitting over there turned away.
If you turn around to sit this way, it will be easier to talk.
Grandmother wiped her tears while sitting turned away.

explain: 앉은 자리에서 몸의 방향만 바꿔 앉는 거예요. 누워서 방향을 바꾸는 '돌아눕다'와 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 등을 돌리고 앉는 모습이라 삐치거나 외면하는 느낌으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means changing your seated direction without moving from your spot. It pairs well in memory with '돌아눕다', which is for lying down. Because you end up with your back turned, it is often used for sulking or avoiding someone.

examples.ko: 산길 옆에 작은 돌탑이 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: A small stone tower is piled up beside the mountain path.

examples.ko: 사찰 마당의 돌탑은 천 년이 넘었대요.
examples.en: They say the stone tower in the temple yard is over a thousand years old.

examples.ko: 사람들이 소원을 빌면서 돌탑에 돌을 하나씩 올려요.
examples.en: People make a wish and place a stone on the tower one by one.
I tried building a stone tower with the kids.

examples.ko: 저는 오래된 돌탑 앞에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo in front of the old stone tower.

examples.ko: 돌탑처럼 높이 쌓인 짐이 무너질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The luggage piled up like a stone tower looks like it will fall.

explain: 돌을 쌓아 만든 탑이에요. 절의 오래된 탑뿐 아니라 산길에서 사람들이 소원을 빌며 하나씩 쌓은 작은 탑도 돌탑이라고 해요. '쌓다'와 같이 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a tower made of piled stones. It covers old temple towers as well as small towers that people pile up one stone at a time along mountain paths while making wishes. It is often used with '쌓다'.

examples.ko: 외국 생활에 대한 동경심이 점점 커졌어요.
examples.en: My longing for life abroad grew bigger and bigger.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 그 선수에게 동경심을 품었어요.
examples.en: I have admired that player since I was little.

examples.ko: 그 도시에 대한 동경심 때문에 이사를 결심했어요.
examples.en: Because of my longing for that city, I decided to move.

examples.ko: 동경심은 직접 겪어 보면 달라지기도 해요.
examples.en: Longing can change once you experience the real thing.
Please don't decide to study abroad based on longing alone.

examples.ko: 작은 동경심에서 시작된 꿈이 진짜 직업이 됐어요.
examples.en: A dream that started from a small longing became a real job.

explain: '동경심을 품다/갖다/느끼다', '동경심이 생기다'처럼 써요. 단순한 부러움보다 어떤 사람이나 세계를 이상적으로 그리며 바라는 마음이 커요.
explain_en: It is used as '동경심을 품다/갖다/느끼다' or '동경심이 생기다'. Rather than plain envy, it is a feeling of yearning toward a person or world that you see as ideal.

examples.en: My eyes went wide with surprise.
The child's eyes go round when they see the present.

examples.ko: 깜짝 놀라 동그래진 눈으로 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: She looked at me with wide, startled eyes.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 들으면 눈이 동그래질 거예요.
examples.en: Your eyes will go wide when you hear the news.

examples.ko: 눈이 동그래지면서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: My eyes went wide and I couldn't say anything.
As you roll the dough it gets rounder and looks pretty.

explain: '둥글어지다'와 비슷하지만 일상에서는 놀라서 '눈이 동그래지다'로 가장 많이 써요. 더 크게 놀랄 때는 '눈이 휘둥그레지다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '둥글어지다', but in daily life it is most often used for eyes going round from surprise, as in '눈이 동그래지다'. For bigger surprise people also say '눈이 휘둥그레지다'.

examples.en: I shape the dough into round balls and bake them.
The baby's cheeks are round and cute.
The stones by the river have been worn round.

examples.ko: 동글동글한 안경을 쓰면 인상이 부드러워 보여요.
examples.en: Wearing round glasses makes you look softer.
I packed the snow into round balls and made a snowman.

examples.ko: 접시에 동글동글 담긴 주먹밥이 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: The round rice balls on the plate look delicious.

explain: 작고 귀여운 둥근 모양을 말할 때 써요. '동글동글하다'로도 쓰고, 더 큰 느낌이면 '둥글둥글'이라고 해요. 사람 성격이 모나지 않을 때는 '성격이 둥글둥글하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a small, cute round shape. It is also used as the adjective '동글동글하다', and the bigger-feeling version is '둥글둥글'. For an easygoing personality you say '성격이 둥글둥글하다'.

examples.en: That person joined the company at the same time as me.
I met my college classmates for the first time in a while.
He was the first of his cohort to get promoted.
We were in the same class at the academy, so we're very close.
The cohort reunion is next month.
People who joined together help each other while working.

explain: 같은 해에 입학하거나 입사한 사람들이에요. 말할 때는 '동기'라고 짧게 많이 해요(예: 우리 동기). '동창'은 같은 학교를 졸업했다는 점이 중심이라 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to people who entered school or joined a company in the same year. In speech people often shorten it to '동기', as in '우리 동기'. '동창' focuses on having graduated from the same school, so it is a bit different.

examples.en: The news of passing spread all over the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 아버지는 동네방네 아들 자랑을 하고 다니세요.
examples.en: My father goes around bragging about his son to everyone.
Please don't spread this around to everybody.
I asked everywhere in the neighborhood to find the cat.
It turns out the rumor had spread everywhere.
We went around telling everyone about the festival.

explain: '퍼지다', '소문내다', '자랑하다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 여기저기 모든 곳이라는 뜻이고 조금 과장해서 말하는 구어체 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It often appears with '퍼지다', '소문내다' and '자랑하다'. It means everywhere, and it has a slightly exaggerated, colloquial feel.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 시내에서 멀리 동떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: This village is far removed from downtown.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 생각은 현실과 너무 동떨어졌어요.
examples.en: His thinking is too far from reality.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 큰길에서 동떨어진 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: Our house is in a place remote from the main road.
If what you say is out of touch with the situation, it's hard to understand.

examples.ko: 그 의견은 사실과 동떨어져서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: That opinion is far from the facts, so it's hard to believe.

examples.ko: 가끔은 세상과 동떨어져 살고 싶을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to live cut off from the world.

explain: 장소가 멀리 떨어져 있을 때뿐 아니라 생각이나 말이 현실과 맞지 않을 때도 써요. 'A와/에서 동떨어지다' 형태로 쓰고, '동떨어진 곳/이야기'처럼 -ㄴ 형태로 뒤에 명사를 꾸미는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is used both for places that are far away and for ideas or words that don't match reality. It takes the pattern 'A와/에서 동떨어지다', and the '-ㄴ' form is common before a noun, as in '동떨어진 곳/이야기'.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 동명이인이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two people with the same name in our class.
We have the same name, so the email went to the wrong person.

examples.ko: 저와 이름이 같은 동명이인을 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: I met someone with the same name as me for the first time.
There are quite a few people with the same names at this school.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 사람은 제 친구와 동명이인이에요.
examples.en: The person in the news just has the same name as my friend.

examples.ko: 동명이인끼리 이름표가 바뀌는 일이 가끔 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes people with the same name get their name tags mixed up.

explain: 이름만 같고 서로 다른 사람을 말해요. '뉴스에 나온 사람은 동명이인이에요'처럼 같은 사람이 아니라는 걸 분명히 할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to different people who happen to share the same name. It is often used to make clear that it's not the same person, as in '뉴스에 나온 사람은 동명이인이에요'.

examples.ko: 동물성 지방은 너무 많이 먹으면 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Eating too much animal fat is not good.
I don't eat animal-based food.

examples.ko: 이 크림에는 동물성 성분이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This cream contains animal-derived ingredients.
Animal protein is plentiful in meat and eggs.
This dish uses only ingredients that are not from animals.

examples.ko: 이 비누는 동물성 원료를 쓰지 않았대요.
examples.en: They say this soap doesn't use animal-derived materials.

explain: 반대말은 '식물성'이에요. 보통 '동물성 지방/단백질/원료'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '식물성'. It is usually placed before another noun, as in '동물성 지방/단백질/원료'.

examples.en: Red flowers bloom on the camellia tree in winter.
There are many camellia trees on Jeju Island.
We planted a camellia tree in our yard.
Flowers had fallen under the camellia tree.
Camellia leaves are thick and shiny.
I walked slowly along the camellia forest path.

explain: 나무 이름이고 꽃은 '동백꽃'이라고 해요. 남쪽 지방에서 잘 볼 수 있고, 겨울과 이른 봄에 피는 꽃으로 유명해요.
explain_en: This is the tree name, and its flower is called '동백꽃'. You can see it often in southern regions, and it is famous for blooming in winter and early spring.

examples.en: This cafe has a very Eastern atmosphere.
I bought a bowl with an Eastern-style pattern.

examples.ko: 이 정원은 동양적으로 꾸민 것 같아요.
examples.en: This garden seems to be decorated in an Eastern style.

examples.ko: 서양적인 방식과 동양적인 방식을 비교해 봤어요.
examples.en: I compared the Western way and the Eastern way.

examples.ko: 그 그림에는 동양적 정서가 잘 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: That painting captures an Eastern sentiment well.
The word 'Eastern' feels different to each person.

explain: 반대말은 '서양적'이에요. '동양적인 느낌/분위기'처럼 쓰는데, 정확한 기준이 있는 말은 아니라서 사람마다 느끼는 게 달라요.
explain_en: The opposite is '서양적'. It is used as in '동양적인 느낌/분위기', but there is no exact standard, so people feel it differently.

examples.ko: 동양화에서는 그림이 없는 여백도 표현의 일부로 여겨요.
examples.en: In Eastern painting, the empty space is also seen as part of the expression.
I saw an Eastern painting exhibition at the art museum.
My grandfather paints Eastern-style paintings as a hobby.

examples.ko: 동양화는 먹과 붓으로 그린 그림이 많아요.
examples.en: Many Eastern paintings are made with ink and brush.

examples.ko: 이 동양화에는 산과 물이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: Mountains and water are painted in this Eastern painting.
Eastern and Western paintings feel very different.

explain: 반대말은 '서양화'예요. 한국에서는 '한국화'라는 말도 많이 쓰고, 보통 먹과 붓으로 그린 그림을 떠올려요.
explain_en: The opposite is '서양화'. In Korea the word '한국화' is also widely used, and people usually picture paintings done with ink and brush.

en: sense of kinship; feeling of similarity

examples.ko: 같은 고향 사람을 만나서 동질감을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a sense of kinship meeting someone from my hometown.
Having a similar experience creates a sense of kinship.
Thanks to that sense of kinship, we quickly became close.

examples.ko: 동질감은 대화가 통할 때 더 커져요.
examples.en: A sense of kinship grows when conversation clicks.
Sometimes friendship starts from a small sense of kinship.
Strangely, I feel a kinship with that singer.

explain: 반대말은 '이질감'이에요. '동질감을 느끼다/들다', '동질감이 생기다'처럼 써요. 나와 비슷하다고 느끼는 마음이라 '공감'과도 가깝지만 같은 점이 있다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '이질감'. It is used as '동질감을 느끼다/들다' or '동질감이 생기다'. It is close to '공감' (empathy), but it puts more weight on feeling that you share something in common.

examples.en: On Dongji day, people eat red bean porridge.

examples.ko: 동짓날은 일 년 중 밤이 가장 길어요.
examples.en: On the winter solstice, the night is the longest of the year.
The winter solstice is near, so I bought ingredients for red bean porridge.
On the morning of the solstice, my mother cooked red bean porridge.
From the winter solstice on, the days slowly get longer.
The rice balls we eat on the solstice are chewy.

explain: 24절기 중 하나인 '동지'가 되는 날이에요. 이날 팥죽에 '새알심'을 넣어 먹는 풍습이 있어요. 옛날에는 팥의 붉은색이 나쁜 기운을 쫓는다고 믿었어요.
explain_en: It is the day of '동지', one of the 24 solar terms. People traditionally eat red bean porridge with '새알심' rice balls on this day. In the past, people believed the red color of the beans drove away bad spirits.

examples.en: In winter, I crave refreshing dongchimi.
I drank a bowl of dongchimi broth.
My mother made dongchimi herself.
I eat noodles with dongchimi broth.

examples.ko: 동치미는 너무 짜지 않게 담가야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Dongchimi tastes good when it isn't made too salty.
This restaurant is famous for its dongchimi cold noodles.

explain: 국물이 많은 물김치의 한 종류로, 겨울에 특히 많이 먹어요. 고구마나 떡과 같이 먹으면 잘 어울려요. '담그다'는 '담가요'처럼 ㅡ가 빠지는 활용이에요.
explain_en: It is a kind of watery kimchi with lots of broth, and people eat it especially in winter. It goes well with sweet potatoes or rice cakes. The verb '담그다' drops its ㅡ in conjugation, as in '담가요'.

examples.en: I climbed the mountain at the break of dawn.
As dawn broke, the sea turned red.

examples.ko: 동터 오는 하늘을 보면서 소원을 빌었어요.
examples.en: I made a wish while watching the sky brighten with dawn.

examples.ko: 날이 밝기 직전, 동트기 전이 제일 어두워요.
examples.en: Right before the day brightens, just before dawn, is the darkest.
As soon as day broke, the farmers went out to the fields.

examples.ko: 날이 막 동텄을 때 우리는 정상에 도착했어요.
examples.en: We reached the summit just as dawn broke.

explain: 해가 뜨기 전에 먼동이 밝아 오기 시작하는 것을 말해요. 해 자체가 뜨는 '해가 뜨다'와 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '날이 밝다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '동이 트다'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes the first light of dawn appearing before the sun rises, which differs from '해가 뜨다' where the sun itself rises. In daily talk '날이 밝다' is more common, and it can also be written as '동이 트다'.

examples.en: It was so cold that the water pipe froze and burst.
When a cold wave comes, water meters freeze and burst.

examples.ko: 물을 조금 틀어 놓으면 동파되지 않아요.
examples.en: If you leave the water running a little, the pipes won't freeze and burst.
I called a repairman to fix the burst pipe.
I'm worried the boiler will freeze and burst.

examples.ko: 겨울에 집을 비울 때는 동파되기 쉬워서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When leaving the house empty in winter, pipes freeze and burst easily, so be careful.

explain: 수도관, 계량기, 보일러처럼 물이 지나가는 것이 얼어서 터질 때 써요. 겨울 한파 뉴스에서 '동파 사고', '동파 방지' 같은 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when something that carries water, such as pipes, water meters or boilers, freezes and bursts. In winter cold-wave news you often hear it in phrases like '동파 사고' and '동파 방지'.

examples.en: I had a dream about pigs last night.
I bought a lottery ticket the day I dreamed about pigs.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈은 재물운이 있다는 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
examples.en: People often say a pig dream means good fortune with money.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈 덕분인지 오늘 일이 잘 풀려요.
examples.en: Maybe thanks to the pig dream, things are going well today.
My friend laughed while telling me about a pig dream.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈이라서 기분이 좋았는데 아무 일도 없었어요.
examples.en: I was happy because it was a pig dream, but nothing happened.

explain: 한국에서는 돼지꿈을 복이나 재물이 들어오는 좋은 꿈으로 여기는 믿음이 있어요. 그래서 돼지꿈을 꾸면 복권을 사 보는 사람도 있어요. '돼지꿈을 꾸다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea there is a belief that a pig dream is a good dream that brings luck or wealth. Some people even buy a lottery ticket after having one. You say '돼지꿈을 꾸다'.

examples.ko: 시골 할아버지 댁 뒤에 돼지우리가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a pigsty behind my grandfather's house in the countryside.
I cleaned the pigsty thoroughly in the morning.
I can hear piglets from the pigsty.
Your room looks just like a pigsty.
The room was as messy as a pigsty, so I cleaned it all up.

examples.ko: 돼지우리 냄새가 심해서 가까이 못 갔어요.
examples.en: The smell of the pigsty was so strong I couldn't go near.

explain: 돼지를 기르는 우리를 말해요. 가축 전체를 기르는 건물은 '축사'라고 해요. 방이 너무 더러울 때 비유로도 쓰는데, 남에게 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 방이나 집이 아주 지저분할 때 쓰는 비유예요. 듣는 사람에게 실례가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a very messy room or house. It can be rude to say to someone.

explain_en: It means the pen where pigs are raised. A building for livestock in general is called '축사'. It is also used figuratively for a very dirty room, but saying it to someone can offend them.

examples.en: Please press the video rewind button.
I rewound it and watched it again from the start.
Videotapes needed to be rewound.
I used rewind to check the scene I missed.
The 10-second rewind function is really convenient.

examples.ko: 되감기가 안 돼서 처음부터 다시 틀었어요.
examples.en: Rewind didn't work, so I played it again from the beginning.

explain: 영상이나 음성을 앞으로 돌려 다시 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. 반대는 '빨리 감기'예요. 요즘은 스트리밍 앱의 '10초 되감기' 버튼에서 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It is used when you go back to replay video or audio. The opposite is '빨리 감기' (fast forward). These days you often see it on the '10초 되감기' button in streaming apps.

examples.en: I rewound the tape to the beginning.
I'll rewind the video a little.
The thread is tangled, so I have to wind it back again.
Do it slowly when you wind the line back.
My hand hurt while I was reeling the fishing line back.

examples.ko: 그 장면까지 되감고 나서 다시 틀어 주세요.
examples.en: Please rewind to that scene and play it again.

explain: 테이프나 실, 줄을 반대로 다시 감을 때 써요. 영상을 앞으로 돌려 보는 것도 '되감다'라고 하고, '되돌리다'도 쓸 수 있어요. 명사형은 '되감기'예요.
explain_en: It is used when winding tape, thread or line back the other way. Going back in a video is also '되감다', and '되돌리다' works too. The noun form is '되감기'.

examples.en: I was in a hurry, so I just threw on whatever and came out.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 있는 걸로 되는대로 만들어 먹어요.
examples.en: I just cook whatever I can with what's in the fridge.

examples.ko: 계획 없이 되는대로 살면 나중에 후회할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you live carelessly without a plan, you may regret it later.

examples.ko: 책을 되는대로 꽂아 두지 말고 정리하세요.
examples.en: Don't just stick the books in anywhere; organize them.

examples.ko: 일단 되는대로 해 보고 안 되면 다시 생각해요.
examples.en: Let's just try it however we can first, and think again if it doesn't work.
I'll contact you as soon as I have time.

explain: '아무렇게나, 대충'이라는 느낌으로 쓸 때와 '가능한 만큼, 가능해지는 대로'라는 뜻으로 쓸 때가 있어요. '시간 되는대로 연락 드릴게요'는 뒤쪽 쓰임이고, 앞뒤 문장을 보면 구별할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It can mean 'carelessly, any old way', or 'as much as possible / as soon as it becomes possible'. '시간 되는대로 연락 드릴게요' is the second use, and the surrounding sentence tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: The road was blocked, so I turned back.

examples.ko: 그는 문 앞에서 갑자기 되돌아서 나갔어요.
examples.en: He suddenly turned around at the door and went out.

examples.ko: 이미 너무 멀리 와서 되돌아설 수는 없어요.
examples.en: We've come too far to turn back.
The moment I was about to turn back, someone called me.
His back as he turned away looked lonely.

examples.ko: 마음을 바꿔 되돌아서면 아직 늦지 않아요.
examples.en: If you change your mind and turn back, it's not too late.

explain: '돌아서다'가 몸의 방향을 바꾸는 것이라면, '되돌아서다'는 왔던 쪽으로 다시 몸을 돌리는 느낌이 있어요. 길을 되돌아갈 때는 '되돌아가다'를 같이 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: While '돌아서다' means simply turning around, '되돌아서다' feels like turning back toward where you came from. When you actually go back along the road, '되돌아가다' is often used alongside it.

examples.ko: 반죽이 너무 되직해서 물을 좀 넣었어요.
examples.en: The dough was too thick, so I added a little water.

examples.ko: 죽이 되직하면 물을 조금 더 부으세요.
examples.en: If the porridge is too thick, pour in a bit more water.
This sauce is on the thick side.

examples.ko: 되직하게 끓여야 밥에 비벼 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: If you boil it thick, it's good for mixing into rice.
The yogurt is thicker than I expected.
The thick dough became soft once I added water.

explain: 반죽, 죽, 소스처럼 물기가 적어 좀 빡빡하고 걸쭉한 느낌에 써요. 반대는 '묽다'예요. '반죽이 되다'와 비슷한 뜻인데, '되직하다'는 '조금 되다'에 가까워요.
explain_en: It is used for batter, porridge or sauce that is a bit stiff and thick because it has little liquid. The opposite is '묽다'. It is close to '반죽이 되다', but '되직하다' means 'somewhat thick'.
